hook_line: There is a specific kind of madness that does not announce itself.
why: Striking opening observation; sets up unwanted intoxication metaphor as the poem's core tension.

hook_line: My heart keeps enjoying the hangover you created, your twinkling eyes, your enlightening smile, your ebony hair.
why: Vivid sensory poetry showing how specific details (not abstractions) stick like involuntary memory.

hook_line: The hangover metaphor works because hangovers have an end point.
why: Reveals the craft: this intoxication refuses to schedule a timeout because it's anchored in particular, real details.

hook_line: Then the moth to flame arrives, and it's not romantic.
why: Reframes attachment as physics (wired, indifferent to consequence) rather than choice or emotion.

hook_line: That's the unsettling thing about attachment: the brain doesn't archive what matters logically.
why: Pivots from metaphor to neuroscience; explains why we can't unstick specific textures, tones, and twinkling eyes.

hook_line: No ground to stand on, no sky to cover my head with.
why: Describes the disorientation when mind and heart collide; you lose the internal coordinates you've always relied on.

hook_line: People realize the mind and heart operate on completely different programming languages when something matters enough.
why: Final insight reframes the breakdown as a signal that something has actually overturned your whole system—which is honest, not a problem.
